definition: A germ cell is a cell in the germline, the reproductive cell line involved in forming eggs or embryos. In this packet, germ cells are discussed as cells that can be damaged by heat shock and protected by stress-response mechanisms.

reasons: The packet does not provide a general definition of “germ cell” as a “reproductive cell line involved in forming eggs or embryos”; it only refers to “oogenic germ cells” and “embryonic lethality,” without explicitly defining germ cells in those terms.

The definition’s framing (“In this packet, germ cells… protected by stress-response mechanisms”) is only partially supported: the packet supports that GLA-3 is important for protecting germ cells from heat shock and involves heat-shock-associated condensates, but it does not clearly support the specific phrasing “protected by stress-response mechanisms.”

The provided field is “mental health,” but the packet content is about molecular/cellular biology in C. elegans (heat shock response), with no mental-health context to justify applying the definition in that field.
The field is not defensible here: the packet is a molecular biology/C. elegans article, not a psychology or counselling source.

The opening gloss broadens the term beyond what the packet states; the packet discusses germ cells in C. elegans germline/gonad, not a general dictionary definition of a germ cell as a reproductive cell line.
The heat-shock/stress-response claim is supported by the packet, but it is only a study-specific finding and should not be framed as a general property of germ cells.
